## 2\. How does our public API work?

Our API exposes a carefully selected set of features, enabling developers to interact with our platform transparently and efficiently. If you'd like to know more about how it works, you can read our official API documentation.

## 3\. How to generate your API keys

API keys are unique identifiers that authenticate requests to our public API. They enable you to programmatically access and manage various resources on our platform.

To connect an external integration, you first need to generate a secure API key. Click on your profile picture and select **Settings** (1). In the left menu, click **MCP & API keys** (2).

Give your key a name, set an expiration date, and click **Save** (4).

Public API

Introduction

Welcome to this comprehensive guide for the Systeme.io Public API. Our API serves as a bridge, enabling developers to interact with Systeme's core functionalities programmatically. It is meticulously designed to offer a seamless integration experience, allowing you to manage contacts, tags, and a variety of other operations integral to our platform. Adhering to RESTful conventions, our API ensures an intuitive and consistent interaction pattern for all users.

Getting Started

To begin using the Systeme.io Public API, you must first obtain an authentication key. This key is your ticket to unlocking the API's capabilities. Simply navigate to the profile settings within your Systeme.io dashboard, and generate a new key under the "Public API keys" section. Once you have your key, you're all set to embark on your first API request journey!
🚧

Important security notice

Using the API from public pages is not advisable as it exposes the API key. This poses a significant security risk. The proper approach is to make API calls from a server-side environment to keep the API key secure. This way, we can avoid CORS issues and maintain the integrity of our system.

Authentication

To authenticate with the Systeme.io Public API, your only option right now is to attach your API key to the X-API-Key header of each request. Let us know which authentication methods you would like to see implemented next!

Rate-Limiting

Our Public API implements a rate-limiting system to maintain service stability and availability for all users. Here's how it works:
* Refill Rate : Your request quota is periodically replenished. The X-RateLimit-Refill header indicates when the next quota refill will occur.

# How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protocol)

The new MCP server feature gives users, partners, and developers a powerful new way to interact with [systeme.io](systeme.io/) using AI tools.

## 1\. Introduction to MCP

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that enables AI assistants (such as ChatGPT or Claude) to connect securely to external platforms.

With MCP, you can use natural language commands to interact with your [systeme.io](systeme.io/) data. For example, you can ask ChatGPT to find a contact or add a tag just by typing a sentence.

Our MCP feature currently provides direct access to specific contact-management features, allowing you to use AI to manage your contacts, tags, and contact fields.

## 2\. How the systeme.io MCP server works

The [systeme.io](systeme.io/) MCP server allows AI applications to access specific contact-management tools within your account.

It creates a bridge between:

* **The host** : Your AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude).
* **The server:** Your [systeme.io](systeme.io/) account.

Once connected, the AI can execute commands to manage your contacts and tags automatically.

For technical details, please refer to our official MCP documentation: <developer.systeme.io/docs/mcp-server>

## 3\. Generating your MCP keys

To connect an AI tool, you first need to generate a secure MCP key.

Click **Settings** (1), then select **MCP & API keys** (2) under **Connections** in the left-hand menu.

Scroll down to the **MCP keys** section and click **Create** (3).

Give your key a name (4), set an expiration date (5), and click **Create** (6).

Your key is now ready.

...

## 5\. Using the systeme.io MCP server

You can use AI tools to perform the following actions:

**a. Contact management:**

* **Create and update contacts:** Add new contacts or update existing ones.
* **Delete contacts:** Remove contacts from your list.
* **List and retrieve contacts:** Use filters to list contacts or fetch specific contact details.
* **Manage tags:** Create, assign, list, and remove tags from contacts.
* **Retrieve contact fields (custom fields):** List available contact fields and their identifiers (slugs) so the AI can correctly fill in and update contact information.

For more information about contact management using the MCP server, check out our dedicated help article: [How to manage your contacts with the](help.systeme.io/article/11331-how-to-manage-your-contacts-with-the-systeme-io-mcp-server) [systeme.io](systeme.io/) [MCP server](help.systeme.io/article/11331-how-to-manage-your-contacts-with-the-systeme-io-mcp-server) .

**b. Newsletter and campaign management:**

* **Newsletters:** Create new drafts, update existing ones, target audiences (using include/exclude tags), configure sender details, schedule or remove scheduling, send test emails, send newsletters directly, delete drafts, and fetch specific newsletters.
* **Campaigns:** Create, retrieve, update, and delete entire email campaigns, as well as individual campaign steps.
* **Email statistics:** Retrieve performance statistics for your newsletters, campaign emails, and automation emails. You can fetch totals for a specific period (up to 31 days) with a daily breakdown, results for each email sent during that period, or all-time results for a specific email. Statistics include sends, opens, clicks, bounces, and spam reports.

...

**k. SMS template management:**

* **Create, edit, and delete:** Generate new SMS templates, or modify and remove existing ones you no longer need.
* **List and search:** Retrieve a list of your existing SMS templates or search for specific ones.

> **Notes:**
> 
> * For security reasons, MCP keys are valid for a maximum of **90 days** .
> * You can create a maximum of **two MCP keys** at a time.
> * This is an **initial release implementation** and does not yet support the recommended authentication method (OAuth). So you may experience minor stability issues.
> * OAuth support **is currently planned** . Once released, it will improve security and eliminate the need for key expiration.
> 
>

excerpts:
How to manage your automation rules and work flows with the systeme.io MCP server

In this article, you will learn how to manage your systeme.io automation rules and workflows using natural language through our native MCP server. By connecting an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude, you can easily create and retrieve simple automation rules to connect common events and actions without configuring them manually in your dashboard.
What you will need:
* A systeme.io account
* An MCP key generated from your systeme.io account ( How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protocol))
* An AI tool connected to your systeme.io account using MCP keys:
* How to connect your systeme.io account with Claude using MCP keys
* How to connect your systeme.io account with ChatGPT using MCP keys

1. Managing automation rules

The MCP server allows you to perform basic actions on your automation rules directly from the chat. You just need to specify the trigger and the action you want the rule to execute.
a. Create an automation rule: You can ask the AI to generate a brand-new automation rule in your account. Currently, the MCP server supports the following specific elements:
* Triggers: Tags (Tag added, Tag removed), Courses (Enrolled in course, Course completed, Lecture completed, Module completed), Sales (Subscription payment failed, New sale, Sale canceled), Funnel form subscribed, Campaign completed, Booking created, and Page visited.
* Actions: Tags (Add a tag, Remove a tag), Courses (Enroll in course, Revoke access to course), Emails (Send email, Send email to a specific address, Subscribe to campaign, Unsubscribe from campaign), Send webhook, and Send SMS.
Example: Create an automation rule that adds the tag "New Lead" when someone subscribes to the "Summer campaign" funnel form.
b. List and retrieve automation rules: You can use the AI to browse through your existing automation rules without having to navigate through your dashboard manually.
Example: List my recent automation rules.

2. Managing workflows

The MCP server allows you to build, manage, and activate automated workflows directly from the chat.
a. Create a workflow: You can ask the AI to generate a workflow and structure its sequence. Currently, the MCP server supports the following specific elements:
* Triggers : Tags (Tag added, Tag removed), Courses (Enrolled in course, Course completed, Lecture completed, Module completed), Sales (Subscription payment failed, New sale, Sale canceled), Funnel form subscribed, Campaign completed, Booking created, and Page visited.
* Actions: Tags (Add a tag, Remove a tag), Revoke access to a course, Subscribe to campaign, Unsubscribe from campaign, Send webhook, Send email to a specific address, and Send SMS.

How to connect your systeme.io account to ChatGPT using MCP keys

In this article, you will learn how to integrate the systeme.io MCP server with ChatGPT so you can interact with your account data using AI.
What you will need:
* A systeme.io account
* An MCP key generated from your systeme.io account ( How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protoco l)
* A ChatGPT account
To connect systeme.io to ChatGPT using an MCP key, log in to your ChatGPT account, open the left side menu, and click Plugins (1).
Click Add (2), and select Add custom MCP server (3).
In the setup popup, enter the following details:
* Name (4): Systeme.io MCP
* Description (optional) (5): Systeme.io official MCP server
* Connection (6): Server URL
* Server URL (7): mcp.systeme.io/mcp?mcpKey=YOUR_KEY
Note: Replace YOUR_KEY with the MCP key you created on your systeme.io account.
* Authentication (8): No Authentication
Tick the I understand and want to continue box (9), then click Create as a plugin (10).
In the "Add Systeme.io MCP server to ChatGPT" window, click Connect systeme.io (11).
Once connected and set up, start a new chat in ChatGPT and start using commands to interact with your systeme.io account.
Notes:
* some actions (like create/update/delete) may be restricted or require additional confirmation. See ChatGPT permissions and action restrictions .
* If the server fails to connect, ensure that:
* Your MCP key is valid and not expired, and you correctly provided it to the server.

# How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protocol)

The new MCP server feature gives users, partners, and developers a powerful new way to interact with systeme.io using AI tools.

Note: The MCP server currently focuses on contact management (contacts, tags, and custom fields), newsletter management, and funnels.

### 1. What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that enables AI assistants (such as ChatGPT or Claude) to connect securely to external platforms.

With MCP, you can use natural language commands to interact with your systeme.io data. For example, you can ask ChatGPT to find a contact or add a tag just by typing a sentence.

Our MCP feature currently provides direct access to specific contact-management features, allowing you to use AI to manage your contacts, tags, and contact fields.

### 2. How does our MCP server work?

The systeme.io MCP server allows AI applications to access specific contact-management tools within your account.

It creates a bridge between:

* The host: Your AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude).
* The server: Your systeme.io account.

Once connected, the AI can execute commands to manage your contacts and tags automatically.

For technical details, please refer to our official MCP documentation: https://developer.systeme.io/docs/mcp-server

### 3. How to generate your MCP keys

To connect an AI tool, you first need to generate a secure MCP key.

Click on your profile picture and select Settings (1).

In the left menu, click MCP & API keys (2).

Scroll down to the MCP keys section and click Create (3).

Give your key a name, set an expiration date, and click Save (4).

Your key is now ready.

### 4. Connect your AI tool

Once you have generated your MCP keys, follow the specific guide below to connect your preferred AI tool to systeme.io:

* How to connect ChatGPT to your systeme.io account using MCP keys
* How to connect Claude to your systeme.io account using MCP keys

### 5. What can you do with our MCP server?

You can use AI tools to perform the following actions:

a. Contact management:

* Create and update contacts: Add new contacts or update existing ones.
* Delete contacts: Remove contacts from your list.
* List and retrieve contacts: Use filters to list contacts or fetch specific contact details.
* Manage tags: Create, assign, list, and remove tags from contacts.
* Retrieve contact fields (custom fields): List available contact fields and their identifiers (slugs) so the AI can correctly fill in and update contact information.

For more information about contact management using the MCP server, check out our dedicated help article: How to manage your contacts with the systeme.io MCP server

b. Newsletter management:

* Create and update newsletters: Generate new newsletter drafts in seconds or update existing ones (including subject lines, preview text, and email content).
* List and retrieve newsletters: Browse through your existing newsletters or find specific ones.

Note on newsletters: Newsletters created via MCP will automatically use the default sender name and email address configured in your account settings (these cannot currently be changed via MCP). Additionally, it is not possible to delete newsletters using MCP tools.

c. Funnel management:

* Create funnels and opt-in steps: Use your AI tool to easily generate new funnels and specific opt-in funnel steps.
* List and retrieve funnels: Browse through your existing funnels and opt-in steps, or search for specific ones.

Note on funnels: Currently, this feature only supports creating and retrieving opt-in funnel steps. Modifying (editing) or deleting funnels and funnel steps via MCP is not supported at this time.

Notes:

* For security reasons, MCP keys are valid for a maximum of 90 days.
* You can create a maximum of two MCP keys at a time.
* This is an initial release implementation and does not yet support the recommended authentication method (OAuth). So you may experience minor stability issues.

The new MCP server feature gives users, partners, and developers a powerful new way to interact with systeme.io using AI tools.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that enables AI assistants (such as ChatGPT or Claude) to connect securely to external platforms.

With MCP, you can use natural language commands to interact with your systeme.io data. For example, you can ask ChatGPT to find a contact or add a tag just by typing a sentence.

Our MCP feature currently provides direct access to specific contact-management features, allowing you to use AI to manage your contacts, tags, and contact fields.

The systeme.io MCP server allows AI applications to access specific contact-management tools within your account.

It creates a bridge between:

The host: Your AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude).

The server: Your systeme.io account.

Once connected, the AI can execute commands to manage your contacts and tags automatically.

For technical details, please refer to our official MCP documentation: https://developer.systeme.io/docs/mcp-server

To connect an AI tool, you first need to generate a secure MCP key.

Click Settings (1), then select MCP & API keys (2) under Connections in the left-hand menu.

Scroll down to the MCP keys section and click Create (3).

Give your key a name (4), set an expiration date (5), and click Create (6).

Your key is now ready.

Once you have generated your MCP keys, follow the specific guide below to connect your preferred AI tool to systeme.io:

How to connect ChatGPT to your systeme.io account using MCP keys

How to connect Claude to your systeme.io account using MCP keys

You can use AI tools to perform the following actions:

a. Contact management:

Create and update contacts: Add new contacts or update existing ones.

Delete contacts: Remove contacts from your list.

List and retrieve contacts: Use filters to list contacts or fetch specific contact details.

Manage tags: Create, assign, list, and remove tags from contacts.

Retrieve contact fields (custom fields): List available contact fields and their identifiers (slugs) so the AI can correctly fill in and update contact information.

For more information about contact management using the MCP server, check out our dedicated help article: How to manage your contacts with the systeme.io MCP server.

b. Newsletter and campaign management:

Newsletters: Create new drafts, update existing ones, target audiences (using include/exclude tags), configure sender details, schedule or remove scheduling, send test emails, send newsletters directly, delete drafts, and fetch specific newsletters.

Campaigns: Create, retrieve, update, and delete entire email campaigns, as well as individual campaign steps.

Email statistics: Retrieve performance
...
binar steps, including registration, thank you, and webinar broadcast pages.

List and retrieve funnels: Browse through your existing funnels, opt-in steps, and webinar pages, or search for specific ones.

Regenerate page content (webinar pages): Regenerate the full content of a webinar page.

For more information about funnel management using the MCP server, check out our dedicated help article: How to manage your funnels with the systeme.io MCP server.

> Notes:

## 2\. How does our public API work?

Our API exposes a carefully selected set of features, enabling developers to interact with our platform transparently and efficiently. If you'd like to know more about how it works, you can read our official API documentation.

## 3\. How to generate your API keys

API keys are unique identifiers that authenticate requests to our public API. They enable you to programmatically access and manage various resources on our platform.

To connect an external integration, you first need to generate a secure API key. Click on your profile picture and select **Settings** (1). In the left menu, click **MCP & API keys** (2).

Scroll down to the Public API keys section and click **Create** (3).

Give your key a name, set an expiration date, and click **Save** (4).

> **Note:** To keep your API key active indefinitely, leave the 'Expiration' field empty.
> 
> 

Your key is now ready.
